data.narrative:
Quantum Art is a Series A quantum computing company that has raised $140M to date. The valuation universe comprises 11 peers across the quantum computing sector: three public companies (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and eight private firms including Quantinuum, IonQ, PsiQuantum, D-Wave Quantum, and SandboxAQ.

The stage-progression method is the applicable triangulation approach here. Using total capital raised ($140M) as a valuation proxy and applying a typical Series A-to-subsequent-stage step-up multiplier of 2.0x yields an implied valuation of $280M. The peer-median method was not applicable due to insufficient comparable data points; while eight same-sector peers exist, filtering for identical stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier produced fewer than three datapoints in any narrow cohort. Reliance on all-sector median metrics would lack sufficient precision.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $238M (low) to $322M (high), with a median estimate of $280M. This range reflects reasonable variance around the stage-progression result given the single-method foundation. Key uncertainties include the lack of tight stage-matched comparables in quantum computing—a sector where funding patterns and valuation inflection points remain volatile—and the reliance on raised capital as a valuation proxy rather than derived multiples on revenue or other operational metrics. Revenue scale and technology maturity vis-à-vis the peer set represent material unknowns affecting precision.
